cohort: 255,233 pregnancies from the 2016 Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project's National Inpatient Sample (HCUP NIS) database
finding: While common combinations of pregestational diagnoses generally do not increase the risk for pregnancy-related complications beyond the risk associated with a single diagnosis, obese patients of advanced maternal age had a 4.4-fold higher risk of preeclampsia compared to patients who were only of advanced maternal age.
